story: At 5:17 on a sunny Monday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Rosa stand on Magnolia Loop, where Gary promises that nothing gets bolted onto any cart until the committee signs off. Hal keeps a watchful eye on the street bulletin board for any Architectural Review notice about cart modifications, while Rosa offers him her removable, strap-on plans and an invitation to join her at the committee tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, Donna is at the Rec Center kiosk, determined to book a two-hour court slot for Gary's practice session.
events: Donna (court reservation kiosk): Check my court booking is two hours max and set for Gary's practice
Hal (street bulletin board): Read the board for any Architectural Review notice on cart modifications

gary.thought_process: Rosa asked me directly if I spotted a Review approval on the board. I scanned it last tick and found nothing, and I filed my own application back at tick 156 with no word yet. Hal's right that nothing gets bolted on until Review signs off, and I'm not about to rig the cart early and give him a reason to write me up. Rosa's offer to walk sketches to the committee is a good one. I should answer her honestly, offer my wiring sketches to go along, and then get back to drawing them up while we wait.

parameters.content: Nothing up on the board yet, Rosa. I filed mine back at the desk but haven't heard a peep. Tell you what, I'll finish my wiring sketches tonight and you can carry both sets to the committee together. Nothing gets bolted on till they sign off, Hal's got my word on that.

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center with the court booked and nobody around yet. I already studied the ladder standings last tick, so rather than stare at the board again, I'll use the kiosk to confirm my two-hour reservation fits the L-05 limit before Gary shows up for practice. Keeps everything by the book, and I'm not repeating myself.

parameters.content: Check my court booking is two hours max and set for Gary's practice

hal.thought_process: Rosa and Gary are both standing here discussing whether Review has posted an approval. I already counted the flamingos and told them nothing gets bolted on until Review posts. I'm not repeating myself. Rosa mentioned she hasn't seen a notice and Gary is scanning the board right now, so the useful move is to check the board myself so there's no guessing. If nothing is posted, I have my answer on record, and I can keep Gary and Donna honest under L-01 and L-02 without anyone being able to claim the paperwork was up.

parameters.content: Read the board for any Architectural Review notice on cart modifications

rosa.thought_process: Hal just asked to see the sketches, and Gary is scanning the board for a Review approval. Hal's been clear: nothing gets built until Review signs off, which matches my plan to keep everything removable. I should engage with Hal directly and not repeat my earlier question to Gary. I'll show Hal the sketches, stress that nothing gets bolted on, and offer to walk them to the committee together. That moves the cart plan forward and keeps the peace with Hal.

parameters.content: Here you go, Hal. Everything's strap-on and removable, nothing touches the cart's frame until Review says yes. If the board's still empty, I'll walk these over to the committee tomorrow morning, and you're welcome to come along.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
